why: 'Agree' is already a verb; don't add 'am'.
Stative verbs like 'have' (possession) are not used in the continuous.
'Know' is not used in the continuous form.

wrong: I have done my graduation in 2022.
why: Use the simple past with a finished time.

right: I am Rahul. / My name is Rahul.
why: 'Myself' is not used as a subject.

wrong: I am doing this since morning.
right: I have been doing this since morning.

wrong: He is my best friend from childhood.
right: He has been my best friend since childhood.

why: 'Do the needful' sounds outdated in formal English.

wrong: I will revert back to you.
right: I will get back to you.
why: 'Revert' already means 'go back'; also it is not the same as 'reply'.

wrong: He gave me a good advice.
She is more smarter than me.
why: Don't use 'more' with a comparative like 'smarter'.

right: He explained the topic to me.

why: Lights are turned on, not opened.

wrong: I am going to my native.
right: I am going to my hometown.
why: 'Native' is not used as a noun for place.

wrong: The team have won the match yesterday.
right: The team won the match yesterday.

wrong: Each of the students have a book.
right: Each of the students has a book.

wrong: I cleared my doubts with the teacher.
right: I got my questions answered by the teacher.
why: 'Clear doubts' is less natural in English.

wrong: I am waiting since two hours.
right: I have been waiting for two hours.

wrong: I am agree to the plan.
